newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded, diesel prices firm.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midcontinent unleaded, diesel prices firm.

text.p: U.S. Midcontinent prompt unleaded gasoline and diesel prices firmed on Wednesday, tracking rising NYMEX prices in morning trade.
Differentials were pegged modestly weaker in Chicago and Group Three on builds in gasoline and distillate stocks, and were expected to fade further against the rallying NYMEX futures, traders said.
"The market is a little weaker, especially the gasoline," one trader said.
Unleaded stocks rose 1.13 million barrels last week in the Midwest PADD II region, where distillate stocks were a modest 176,000 barrels higher, the American Petroleum Institute reported.
Refineries in the region were operating at 88.1 percent of capacity, down 2.4 percentage points on the week, traders said.
Chicago winter-grade unleaded gasoline was talked 9.0/8.75 cents a gallon under NYMEX April unleaded, with summer-grade unleaded about 7 cents firmer, traders said.
Group Three unleaded was steady at 2.50/2.75 cents a gallon under the print for prompt barrels, with later deliveries 0.25 cent a gallon weaker.
Chicago low sulphur diesel was steady at bids 3.75 cents a gallon over April NYMEX heating oil for prompt deliveries and 3.50 cents a gallon over the print for later deliveries.
Group Three low sulphur diesel was bid 5.25 cents a gallon over the print for prompt deliveries and remained 0.25 cent weaker for later deliveries, traders said.
High sulphur diesel was talked 2.25 cents a gallon over the print in Chicago and 0.25 cent weaker in Group Three.
